newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - May 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - May 23.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Under a radical Federal Government plan outlined by Department of Prime Minister and Cabinet head Max Moore-Wilton, Australia's car industry may benefit from a five-year freeze on tariff cuts and heavily reduced wholesale sales taxes. The plan would see passenger motor vehicle tariffs remain at 15 percent from 2000 to 2005 rather than lowered to five percent as recommended by the Industry Commission. Page 1.

Australian Bureau of Statistics wages figures released yesterday may work in combination with this week's U.S. Federal Reserve decision not to raise interest rates, and could see the Reserve Bank of Australia cutting official interest rates. The ABS figures showed wages growth is under control. Page 1.

Following a three-year programme of internal cost-stripping, Qantas Airways managing director James Strong has announced a A$560 million upgrade of its in-flight operations. The upgrade will be phased in by 2000 and will be introduced to ensure the airline's competitive edge in both domestic and overseas markets. Page 41.

Qantas Airways executive general manager commercial Geoff Dixon said yesterday the airline may not go ahead with negotiations to acquire a half share in Australia's biggest travel group Jetset. An announcement on the outcome of the talks is expected next week. Page 41.

In a surprise announcement, West Australian Resources Minister Colin Barnett said the West Australian Government will privatise the A$1.2 billion Dampier to Bunbury natural gas pipeline. In what would be the biggest privatisation in the state's history, Barnett said the sale strategy would "honour the integrity" of the gas deregulation process. Page 43.

Australian Gas Association executive director Ian Woodward said yesterday that reform of Australia's natural gas industry, that would remove interstate trading barriers and create a free and fair national market, has been too slow for the needs of a "dynamic" national gas market. Page 43.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Under a deal believed to have been signed in the past few weeks, the Seven Network has poached the programming of Hollywood film and television powerhouse Universal Studios, the key supplier of content to the Ten Network. While the deal is expected to weaken Ten's future programming, it will not take effect for another three years. Page 23.

Under the first step in a major restructuring plan of its Magma Copper assets acquired in late 1996, BHP will slice up to 500 jobs from the Arizona-based San Manuel copper operations. The troubled San Manuel comprises the largest underground copper mine in the United States and a 1.2 million tonnes-a-year smelter. Page 23.

Qantas managing director James Strong said yesterday a A$550 million relaunch of Qantas announced yesterday was "fundamental to the competitive position" of the airline. The relaunch will include inflight systems in every seat that can offer gambling facilities, a new TV advertising campaign and new seating. Page 23.

Union Mining managing director Rob Murdoch told the Australian Stock Exchange yesterday the company has found a further potential gold resource on PNG's Fergusson Island in Milne Bay. The finding followed a study of the results of a first phase drill program at its Igwageta prospect. Page 24.

Foster's Brewing Group and Pacific Dunlop chairman John Ralph said yesterday at the Australian Institute of Company Directors national conference in Melbourne that there must be a far-reaching inquiry into the issue of tax reform. Ralph said the inquiry should be a thorough as the Wallis inquiry into the banking sector. Page 25.

A survey by Teltech Enterprises and commissioned by cost analysis firm NUS International shows companies are not prepared for the deregulation of the telecoms sector, with close to a quarter either receiving no discount on their phone bill or unaware of whether they will receive any discount. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Qantas QAn.AX managing director James Strong said yesterday the airline would spend over A$550 million upgrading its products and services over the next three years to give itself an internatioanl edge. The figure of A$550 million is over the forecasted amount of A$450 million outlined last year, yet the new spending was approved by the board in the past month. Page 27.

The proposal to sell off New South Wales' electricity sector may also see several power businesses sold, and should attract foreign investment. The sales, expected to raise up to A$25 billion, will probably create one or more cross-border electricity operators with assets in both New South Wales and Victoria. Page 27.

Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Professor Allan Fels indicated yesterday there may be troubles for the Westpac takeover of the Bank of Melbourne, saying a substantial lessening of competition in just one area of product - home loans, deposits, and transaction accounts - would be enough for the takeover to be rejected under the Trade Practices Act. Page 27.

Despite reports early this week that talks between Telstra and Optus had fallen through, Optus Communications is still keen to push for the two companies to share their multi-billion dollar cable networks. Optus chief executive Ziggy Switkowski said yesterday a deal between the two would help the pay TV industry. Page 29.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission and the Bureau of Meteorology jointly announced yesterday an agreement had been reached after the ACCC claimed the Bureau had abused its position as the sole provider of weather information by denying infrmation to a potential competitor, New Zealand based MetService. Page 29.

Life Investment and Superannuation Association chairman Dr Peter Jonson says the body supports the Federal Government's budget measures to provide relief on savings. Jonson said the A$450 rebate was a welcome move that will have a noticeable effect over he next two or three years. Page 29.
THE AGE

NSW Treasurer and Energy Minister Michael Egan has presented a discussion paper to unions at generation company Pacific Power outlining plans for a A$22 billion, debt dissolving power sell-off. In a move that mirrors that of the Victorian Government, the sale should rid the state of its debt and provide budget savings of around A$500 million a year. Page B1.

Qantas head James Strong announced yesterday A$550 million will be spent over three years to attract increasingly demanding air travellers. New seats, sleeper seats on international flights, and specially trained flight attendants in first class make up he upgrade plan. Page B1.

Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Professor Allan Fels believes there will be more action against government departments following a joint announcement between the ACCC and the Bureau of Meteorology that they had settled legal action alleging the Bureau had abused its powers. Page B1.

Australian Institute of Company Directors chairman John Ralph said yesterday the business community had to move away from the adversarial system of reform and work with the government to gain common objectives from tax reform. He said reform had to be moe wide-ranging than just introducing a goods and services tax. Page B1.

National Mutual Holdings' 69 percent owned Asian subsidiary, National Mutual Asia, has reported a A$98.2 million interim profit. Managing director Terry Smith said that despite analysts predicting lower investment returns and increased competition would hurt National Mutual Asia, the company's new life business was up by 14.3 percent. Page B3.

Bendigo Bank managing director Rob Hunt said yesterday the proposed A$1.44 billion merger of Westpac and Bank of Melbourne would allow Bendigo to expand its market share in Melbourne. Managing director Rob Hunt said there would be enough customers leaving Bank of Melbourne for Bendigo "to do very nicely". Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
